title_en: A Trance of Devotion (Bhava-Samadhi) in Jagannath Puri
translation:
Bhava-Samadhi in Jagannath Puri

By the command of Guru Gopaldasji, Jivanji Maharaj set out with him from Chorenda toward Malwa on the tenth day of the bright half of Aso, in Vikram Samvat 1687. But in Malwa, since the financial condition of Gopaldasji's friend was not sufficient to support both guru and disciple, Jivanji Maharaj sought leave from Guru Gopaldas and travelled on ahead alone. On the way, afflicted by hunger, Jivanji Maharaj ate the fruit of the beheda tree. Having eaten too much of the fruit,

he became intoxicated by it and fell unconscious, remaining so for some time beneath that very tree. At this time, a company of saints happened to be passing on their way to pilgrimage at Jagannath Puri; they saw Jivanji Maharaj lying unconscious, and this company of saints then brought him along with them to Jagannath Puri. He remained there for some days. One evening, in the presence of Lord Jagannath, Jivanji Maharaj slipped into bhava-samadhi (a trance of devotional absorption), losing all awareness of time. In this state he remained seated, leaning against a pillar. As night fell, the temple's attendants and priests closed the temple doors and went home.

Jivanji Maharaj lay absorbed in bhava-samadhi, with no awareness of time at all. At midnight, hearing the sound of someone moving about on every side, he awoke from his trance and began looking around, only to realize that he was shut inside the temple. He could see no one, yet he heard the sound of someone's footsteps. This episode in the life of Jivanji Maharaj is described by Shyamdasji, who writes:

_Sandhya same aarti bhai, mandirmen baithe sukhamai._
_Aarti kari sab uthike chale, sej sanvaarine paande mile. ||9||_
_Sej sanvaari prabhu podhai, sabai chale charan sir naai._
_Sadguru Jeevan rahe lukaai, taaki kaahu khabar na paai. ||10||_
(At evening time the aarti was performed, and the deity sat there in bliss within the temple. After the aarti, all rose and departed; the priests arranged the resting-couch and then took their leave. ||9|| Having arranged the couch and settled the Lord to rest, all bowed their heads at His feet and departed. Sadguru Jivan[a] remained hidden there, and no one came to know of it. ||10||)

According to a popular belief, no one may spend the night inside the Puri temple; it is said that anyone who stays there overnight will either die or lose his sanity. But Jivanji Maharaj disproved this belief — nothing of the kind happened to him; he neither died nor went mad.
